sections.h2: Where does Effingham County fit in the Savannah area?
sections.html:
Effingham sits on the northwest side of metro Savannah, bordered by Chatham, Bryan and Bulloch counties in Georgia and by Hampton and Jasper counties across the river in South Carolina. Springfield holds the courthouse, while Rincon is the biggest town. Guyton is the third city, and Clyo, Egypt, Meldrim and Shawnee are unincorporated communities (Wikipedia).

Georgia created the county on February 5, 1777, which makes it one of the original ones, and Springfield dates to 1799. Part of the Savannah National Wildlife Refuge lies inside the line. In 2008 the Census Bureau ranked Effingham the sixth-fastest-growing midsize county in the nation for 2000 to 2007, with a 35.1 percent jump.

That growth continues in the QuickFacts figures: 64,769 people at the 2020 count, 74,397 estimated by July 2025, and 212 building permits in 2025. Homes are valued at a median $276,000, households earn a median $88,438, and workers spend 32.3 minutes getting to their jobs. Roughly 78 of every 100 homes are lived in by their owners.

sections.h2: Which two offices decide an Effingham County property tax bill?
sections.html:
The Board of Tax Assessors puts a value on each parcel, and the Tax Commissioner turns that value into a bill and collects it. The commissioner's own page stresses that it sets neither values nor millage. Rates come from the Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education.

sections.h2: What does the 2026 Effingham tax bill look like after the county's relief?
sections.html:
The county advertised a package it calls Project Zero, and the numbers are large. A county news item from September 22, 2026 said bills for tax year 2026 had been mailed and posted online, with homestead property seeing about 30 percent in total savings and other property about 20 percent.

Here is where that relief came from, per the same notice:

  • The county cut its millage by 2 mills.
  • The school district cut its millage by 2 mills.
  • The county industrial development authority suspended its 2-mill levy.
  • Qualifying homesteads also receive a state grant.

All of that traces to the Project Camellia land sale. A referendum on a Local Homeowners Incentive Adjustment Grant went before voters in November 2026, and if approved it would let the county use available funds to erase county tax on qualifying homesteads in 2027. Read the result on effinghamtax.com before pricing a 2027 sale. Voters also turned down a six-year SPLOST renewal by 140 votes in the same election, per the commissioner's site.

sections.h2: When does Effingham County expect payment, and how fast do penalties build?
sections.html:
Bills for real estate normally come due on November 20. Mobile homes follow a spring schedule, and the commissioner's page gives May 1.

The tax FAQ sets out a ladder of consequences:

  • One percent interest per month starts accruing the day after November 20.
  • Every 120 days adds 5 percent, with a cap at 20 percent overall.
  • Once taxes run past 90 days, the commissioner may record a fi. fa. with the court clerk, and credit bureaus can read it.
  • Levy on the property is the last resort, which the office says it would rather avoid.

The FAQ also reminds owners that bills are addressed to them and never to a lender, so anyone with an escrow account should forward theirs. You can pay by e-check online for a $2 processing fee, which the commissioner contrasts with higher card fees.

sections.h2: How do you challenge an Effingham County value?
sections.html:
You contest a value by appealing within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. The county FAQ names two routes, the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, with superior court available after either decision.

Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value, taken as of January 1 each year. The commissioner subtracts exemptions, then multiplies what remains by the millage rate, where one mill equals one dollar per $1,000 of assessed value.

On filing, the assessors accept appeals and waivers only by mail or hand delivery to 802 S. Laurel Street, North Administration Complex. A taxpayer holding a no-change notice who prefers to skip the hearing can submit a waiver until a hearing date is set. A green postcard means an appraiser may visit your area within 60 days under state law, and no response is needed.

sections.h2: What homestead exemptions does Effingham County list?
sections.html:
The county publishes its own schedule, and a local amount overrides the state amount whenever it is larger. Its exemption page breaks the types down this way:

  • Regular (S1): $4,000 for county tax and $2,000 for school tax.
  • Ages 62 to 64, income-tested (S3): $4,000 county and $10,000 school.
  • Age 65 and older (SC): $4,000 county and $12,000 school.
  • Age 65 and older, income-tested (S4): $6,000 county, $20,000 school, and $100 off the sanitation bill.
  • 100 percent disabled veteran (S5) and VA surviving spouse (SS): $101,754.

You qualify by owning and living in the home on January 1, and applications must land by April 1 for that year. The county also takes applications online. It also warns that retitling a home to an LLC, renting out part of it, or claiming a second exemption elsewhere can end the exemption, and a double claim can draw a fine of two times the savings for up to three years.

sections.h2: How should an Effingham County owner handle a sale when tax is behind?
sections.html:
A sale removes the seller's exemption, since the county lists a sold property as grounds for removal, and the buyer applies for a new one. Before you list, get a balance in writing from the commissioner for every open year.

  • Clear old years from the proceeds so no lien rides along with the title.
  • Agree in the contract on who covers the 2026 bill.
  • Stop any lender escrow after payoff.

Unpaid years can end in a public sale. The commissioner advertised a December 2026 tax sale for Tuesday, December 1, at 804 South Laurel Street between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Property goes for cash or certified funds, as is, with rights of redemption, and the buyer pays for title, transfer, advertising and recording. Parcels leave the list when an owner pays, so the advertised list changes up to the sale.

A seller facing a sale date can choose a faster cash closing. Effingham's $276,000 median home value is far above the $94,700 to $142,000 medians for Elbert, Emanuel and Evans counties, so there is often equity to protect.

faqs.q: What is the Effingham County deadline for paying the regular bill?
faqs.a: November 20 is the usual date, per the tax commissioner's FAQ. Interest begins the next day at 1 percent per month. Pay online, by phone at 470-531-3402, or at the office.

faqs.q: Who accepts homestead applications in Effingham County?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor's office does, and it also takes them online. File by April 1 or the exemption starts the following year. First-time owners should bring a copy of the warranty deed.

faqs.q: Is it too late to dispute a 2026 Effingham County value?
faqs.a: Probably. The window runs 45 days from the date printed on each notice, and for most owners that period has ended. File promptly after the next notice, and call 912-754-2125 for the right form.

faqs.q: Does a new Effingham County owner inherit my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The county removes the exemption after a sale, and the new owner applies. Seniors and veterans must also reapply for the higher categories.

faqs.q: What happens at an Effingham County tax sale?
faqs.a: The ex-officio sheriff sells levied parcels at public outcry for cash or certified funds. Sales are as is and subject to redemption rights, and the buyer pays title, transfer, advertising and recording costs.
